decoy_bugs.summary: scan_entity does not range-check decimal numeric character references, so a reference above U+10FFFF such as � is decoded to a wrong scalar value instead of U+FFFD.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: A decimal numeric character reference whose value is above 0x10FFFF but has at most 7 digits (e.g. � or �) comes out in the Text event as a character other than U+FFFD, or the reference is dropped.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: scan_entity (scanners.rs:906) passes the parse_decimal(&bytes[end..], 7) result at line 914 to char_from_codepoint at line 922, and an out-of-range codepoint is reduced instead of being rejected there.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by:
Ran a probe example through ./run (cargo run --example probe on a copy in tmp/crate) rendering "� � � �": the output was

� � � �

. Each one became U+FFFD, because char_from_codepoint calls char::from_u32, which returns None for out-of-range and surrogate values, and scan_entity then falls back to unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}').

decoy_bugs.summary: In a pointy-bracket link destination, a backslash-escaped \> ends the destination early, so [a](<b\>c>) does not produce a link to b>c.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: An inline link or link reference definition whose <...> destination contains \> is cut off at the escaped bracket: the href becomes 'b\' or no link is produced, and the rest shows up as literal text.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: The pointy branch of scan_link_dest (scanners.rs:962-972) matches b'>' at line 965 before it accounts for the preceding backslash escape, so an escaped > closes the destination.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by:
The probe through ./run rendered "[a](c>)" and "[a]\n\n[a]: c>". Both gave

a

, the full destination b>c. Reading the code: at line 966 the backslash arm advances i past the escaped punctuation byte, so the escaped > is never tested against line 965.

false_findings.text:
**Sign-extended SIMD mask drives get_unchecked past the buffer**
pulldown-cmark/src/firstpass.rs:2715 (process_mask).
With the simd feature enabled, input whose 16-byte block has a special byte in the last lane makes process_mask call the callback with an offset beyond bytes.len(), which is an out-of-bounds read through get_unchecked.
The mask is an i32 from _mm_movemask_epi8, and the arithmetic `mask >>= shift` at line 2722 copies the sign bit into the cleared high bits, so trailing_zeros keeps producing new offsets after the real lanes are used up.
A build with --features simd showed the callback receiving offset == bytes.len() + 1 on a 31-byte input ending in `*`, with debug_assert disabled.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Read compute_mask: _mm_movemask_epi8 sets only the low 16 bits, so the mask is never negative and an arithmetic shift cannot bring in set bits. Then ran a differential probe through ./run: 200,000 pseudo-random inputs of 0-119 chunks drawn from all special bytes plus multibyte characters, with Options::all(), as a debug build with and without --features simd. The output hashes were identical (ba3509aba645d3fc, total length 25732491), and there were no panics or debug_assert failures.

false_findings.text:
**Uppercase-X hex character references left undecoded** pulldown-cmark/src/scanners.rs:910 (scan_entity). A hexadecimal numeric reference written with a capital X, such as `&` or `A`, is not decoded and is emitted as the literal text `&`, unlike its `&` form, which breaks CommonMark spec example 26. The hex branch checks for b'x' only, so `&#X` falls through to parse_decimal, which reads zero digits and makes scan_entity return (0, None). Rendering `a & b &` with push_html produced `

a & b &

`.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by:
Line 910 tests `bytes[end] | 0x20 == b'x'`, which folds case. The probe through ./run rendered "a & b & c A" as

a & b & c A

, so both forms decode the same way.

false_findings.text:
**Nine-digit ordered list marker at end of input panics**
pulldown-cmark/src/scanners.rs:830 (scan_listitem).
A document that ends right after a 9-digit ordered list marker, e.g. the 10-byte input `123456789.` or `123456789)`, panics with a slice index out of range instead of producing an empty list item.
parse_decimal(bytes, 9) returns length 9, and w = length + 1 then slices `&bytes[w..]` for calc_indent without checking that a byte follows the delimiter.
Running `printf '123456789.' | pulldown-cmark` aborted with "range start index 10 out of range for slice of length 10".
false_findings.confirmed_false_by:
Line 819 uses `bytes.get(length)?`, so the delimiter byte exists and w <= bytes.len(), which makes &bytes[w..] an empty but valid slice. The probe through ./run rendered "123456789." and "123456789)" each as
with no panic. A 10-digit marker correctly stays a paragraph.

false_findings.text:
**Quadratic label normalization on leading whitespace**
pulldown-cmark/src/linklabel.rs:147 (scan_link_label_rest).
A link label that opens with a long run of mixed spaces and tabs, such as `[` followed by 100k copies of ` \t` and then `x]`, takes time quadratic in the run length while the label is normalized.
The leading-trim loop calls `label.remove(0)` once per whitespace byte, and each call shifts the whole remaining String.
Timing push_html on that input rose from 0.9 ms at n=10^4 to about 9 s at n=10^5.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: Read the whitespace arm (lines 90-117): a whole whitespace run is pushed as a single ' ', so the remove(0) loop runs at most once, and the codepoints >= 1000 guard stops long labels. The timing probe through ./run measured n=10^3/10^4/10^5/10^6 at 14 µs / 101 µs / 935 µs / 14.5 ms, which is linear. 10^5 copies of a whitespace-padded label took 48 ms.

false_findings.text:
**Heading id written into HTML without escaping** pulldown-cmark/src/html.rs:182 (HtmlWriter::start_tag). With ENABLE_HEADING_ATTRIBUTES, a heading id that contains a double quote, such as `# h {#a"onmouseover=x}`, closes the id attribute and adds an attacker-controlled attribute to the generated

. The Tag::Heading arm writes `id` straight to the writer with write!, while classes and attrs go through escape_html. Rendering that line with push_html gave `

h

`.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by:
Lines 181-184 call escape_html(&mut self.writer, &id), the same as classes and attrs. The probe through ./run rendered "# h {#a\"onmouseover=x .c\"d data-x=\"y\"}" with ENABLE_HEADING_ATTRIBUTES as

h

, with every quote escaped.
